fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline titanium alloy is unrelated to the target equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
No specific titanium composition, processing history, crystal structure, orientation, or supporting evidence is provided.
The tensile conditions of 20–500 °C do not reconstruct the target single-crystal compression experiments spanning 9–1373 K.
The monotonic prediction of increased plastic deformation with temperature misses the observed cryogenic inertial dulling and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier strengthening.
Grain-boundary sliding and grain-size mediation are inappropriate to the central single-crystal mechanisms examined in the target study.
explanation: The hypothesis is a generic, scientifically possible statement about titanium alloys, but it neither reconstructs nor evidentially supports the target material system. It omits the composition-dependent MSAD strengthening, phonon-drag-controlled inertial regime, Mn/Fe-associated solute pinning, CRSS measurements, strain-rate jumps, and TEM/DFT tests. Room temperature is a reasonable baseline and temperature-dependent mechanical testing could test the broad claim, but the proposed falsification rule is vague and does not distinguish among relevant deformation mechanisms.
